documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page offers sample syllabus statements at three levels (permissive, mixed-use, unpermitted) plus an optional required-AI addition, and says "Faculty can create customized AI policies for each course", so it sets no single stance and delegates to instructors via tiers.
tiers: Optional addition: AI required for some assignments
documents.summary: A university AI office page giving faculty template syllabus statements for student AI use, from permissive-with-disclosure to unpermitted, plus an optional required-AI clause. It also sets a FERPA-based student data protection statement that binds faculty use of AI.

units.why: Rationale for syllabus AI policies: "set clear expectations" and "protects academic integrity while encouraging innovation". It urges adding AI statements to courses, so P09; framed as a benefit rather than an order, hence should.
units.anchor: Adding AI policies to courses helps set clear expectations for students
units.fit_note: Framed as a benefit of syllabus statements rather than an explicit requirement.

units.why: Warns that without guidelines students "may be confused" and commit "unintentional violations or missed learning opportunities"; explains the need for explicit expectations, so communication rationale (P09) rather than a stance.
units.anchor: Without clear guidelines, students may be confused about what AI use is acceptable
units.fit_note: Rationale for stating expectations, not the requirement itself.

units.why: "Faculty are expected to abide by these restrictions on their own AI use, regardless of whether the statement is included in their syllabus" binds faculty to the data-protection limits; P50 protects student data.
units.anchor: Faculty are expected to abide by these restrictions on their own AI use

units.why: "explicit written consent, as required under FERPA" before faculty enter student data into a third-party AI tool: a data-protection rule for faculty, P50 (not P20, which concerns students).
units.anchor: unless you give explicit written consent, as required under FERPA

units.why: "data-minimization principle - only the smallest amount of information possible" limits what faculty share with AI tools; privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: only the smallest amount of information possible will be used

units.why: "Any vendor employed by the university must have FERPA" compliant data-protection policies: sets vendor vetting and transparency, matching P65 (review of AI tools and vendors).
units.anchor: Any vendor employed by the university must have

units.why: "You will be informed about what data (if any) is shared, provided, or stored when we use any AI tool in the classroom" commits instructors to tell students about their AI tool use; P47 (disclose instructor AI use).
units.anchor: You will be informed about what data (if any) is shared
units.fit_note: Disclosure concerns data shared with AI tools used in class, not only grading or feedback.

units.why: "and you can opt out" gives students a right to opt out of classroom AI tool use, a choice protection; nearest is P51 (AI optional, alternatives).
units.anchor: and you can opt out.
units.fit_note: Opt-out concerns instructor-chosen AI tools that process student data, not student AI use.

units.why: "Faculty can create customized AI policies for each course based on their teaching goals" leaves the decision to instructors; P04 is primary (P83, objectives, is secondary).
units.anchor: Faculty can create customized AI policies for each course

units.why: "AI-intensive courses may require detailed policies, while others might prohibit the use of AI entirely" notes the range from detailed policy to full prohibition; informs on variation, P04.
units.anchor: while others might prohibit the use of AI entirely

units.why: "Since AI violations can be hard to detect, requiring students to disclose AI usage may be more practical than outright bans" admits detection limits and prefers disclosure to bans; P82 fits best, disclosure preference noted.
units.anchor: Since AI violations can be hard to detect
units.fit_note: Also recommends disclosure requirements over bans (P24).

units.why: Heading "Permissive & Reflective Policy (AI encouraged with disclosure)" with the mixed-use and unpermitted samples names categories of AI policy; P05 names tiers.
units.anchor: Permissive & Reflective Policy (AI encouraged with disclosure)
units.fit_note: Three sample statements: permissive, mixed-use, unpermitted.

units.why: "You are invited to use AI tools strategically in this course" welcomes AI use in the permissive sample; P02.
units.anchor: You are invited to use AI tools strategically in this course
units.policy: You are invited to use AI tools strategically in this course to brainstorm, draft, analyze, or revise.

units.why: "to brainstorm, draft, analyze, or revise" lists permitted uses; brainstorming is the specific permission, P15, though drafting and revising go wider.
units.anchor: to brainstorm, draft, analyze, or revise
units.fit_note: Also permits drafting, analyzing and revising, not only brainstorming.

units.why: "briefly explain how you used the tool" in a note or method section requires disclosure with the submission, naming tool and use; P24.
units.anchor: briefly explain how you used the tool

units.why: "If you choose not to use AI in your learning process, that is perfectly acceptable" makes AI optional in the permissive policy, a choice protection; P51.
units.anchor: If you choose not to use AI in your learning process
units.frag_start: If you choose not to use

units.why: "You are responsible for the accuracy and ethics of any artificial intelligence outputs" makes students answerable for output quality; P31 with the ownership aspect noted. Repeated in three samples; coded once.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the accuracy and ethics of any artificial intelligence outputs
units.fit_note: States responsibility for accuracy and ethics rather than an explicit duty to verify.

units.why: "For specific assignments (not all), AI may be used" but only if permitted in the assignment instructions: a per-assignment permission; P04.
units.anchor: AI may be used

units.why: "to generate research questions or draft outlines" gives example permitted uses in the mixed-use policy, brainstorming and outlining; P15.
units.anchor: to generate research questions or draft outlines
units.fit_note: Examples only; permission applies only where assignment instructions allow.

units.why: "When permitted, you must cite your usage" requires a citation of AI use; P24.
units.anchor: When permitted, you must cite your usage

units.why: "any assignment lacking explicit AI permissions" must be own work: sets the fallback when permission is silent; P06.
units.anchor: any assignment lacking explicit AI permissions

units.why: "must be entirely your own work, without AI tools" states ownership of work and the ban on AI for unpermitted work; P29.
units.anchor: must be entirely your own work, without AI tools
units.fit_note: Own-work requirement framed as a ban on AI tools for unpermitted assignments.

units.why: "If you are uncertain whether AI is allowed on a task, reach out for clarity" tells students to ask when unsure; P10.
units.anchor: reach out for clarity before submitting your work
units.frag_start: If you are uncertain whether AI

units.why: "you will be expected to use AI in pursuit of the course learning objectives" is the optional addition for courses that expect AI use; P79 requires AI in coursework.
units.anchor: you will be expected to use AI in pursuit of the course learning objectives
units.frag_start: For one or more assignments in

units.why: "the use of AI remains optional" with "accommodations or alternative assignments" preserves choice for required-AI assignments; P51.
units.anchor: accommodations or alternative assignments can be made
units.frag_start: the use of AI remains optional

units.why: "you are required to use AI in the ways detailed by the professor" is the alternative statement making AI use mandatory; P79.
units.anchor: you are required to use AI in the ways detailed by the professor

notes: The faculty-handbook academic integrity page has no AI text, so not collected. No school or computing-unit policy found (Mathematics and Computer Science searched). Repeated accuracy-and-ethics sentence coded once.
